text:
incident-bot: Paging oncall-amber — multiple websocket stream timeouts (502/504) reported for tenant cobaltbridge in the eu-west dedicated VPC pool. Error rate spike ~12x starting ~10:08 UTC. Paging P1 if customer impact. :rotating_light:
oncall-amber: Acknowledged. I'm on it. Can someone grab metrics and list affected endpoints?
kyra: I'm seeing elevated backend grpc timeouts for /stream/ingest and /stream/subscribe from the cobaltbridge pool. 95th latency jumped from 120ms -> 2.6s.
matt-lee: Logs show a burst of `read: connection reset by peer` and `write timeout` on the app-gateway side starting 10:07:54. Possible upstream slow drain.
devops-jay: Confirmed. Dedicated pool dedicated-cobalt has GPU utilization at 96% and kernel queueing. Could be KV-cache thrash from long-lived sessions.
cobalt-sre: We're seeing many client reconnects from our side, ~30% of sessions failing to reconnect within 5s. No recent deploys on our end. We'll keep our clients paused if you want to test.
oncall-amber: Quick mitigation options: 1) route cobaltbridge traffic to standby dedicated pool (if available), 2) temporarily increase gateway ws idle timeout and relax strict keepalive, 3) apply token-level rate-limit to throttle extreme retries from clients. Which should we do first?
shaun: Standby pool exists: dedicated-cobalt-standby. We can failover route in ~2-3m but need to ensure KV cache warmup will be cold and may increase latency for a bit.
kyra: I'd prefer rate-limit + client backoff ask first to avoid cold start. Also can we drop persistent batching for that tenant (reduces memory spike)?
matt-lee: We should also adjust connection backlog at the app-gateway: `sysctls/net.core/somaxconn` bump and threadpool size +1 for gateway process to reduce accept churn.
devops-jay: Command ready for quick routing test: 
```
# route cobaltbridge to standby pool (dry-run show)
redwoodctl route get --tenant cobaltbridge --env eu-west
redwoodctl route set --tenant cobaltbridge --pool dedicated-cobalt-standby --weight 100 --dry-run
# when ready (remove --dry-run)
```
oncall-amber: Matt, can you apply the sysctl tweak and restart gateway workers on eu-west edge nodes? I'll coordinate the rate-limit and routing.
matt-lee: Applying sysctl + rolling restart now on 6 nodes. Should be ~60s per node, doing one at a time.
eng-ops-bot: Deploy kickoff: rolling-restart/gateway/eu-west started by matt-lee at 10:18 UTC.
kyra: I'm pushing a tenant-scoped rate limit: 50 rps sustained with 10 burst for cobaltbridge on the eu-west gateway. This will reject with 429 and instruct clients to backoff.
cobalt-sre: We can add jitter to client retry and reduce parallel reconnects, pushing a config now. Expect client behavior to change within seconds.
oncall-amber: Monitoring: error-rate dropping from 12x -> 4x since rate-limit. Gateway accept queue depth lowered after sysctl tweak.
shaun: Standby route ready as fallback. If errors don't drop to near baseline in 5m we flip route.
matt-lee: Two nodes finished restart, rest ongoing. No increased error logs so far, accept churn improved.
eng-ops-bot: Metric alert cleared (ws-error-rate) for cobaltbridge in eu-west at 10:27 UTC — was triggered at 10:09 UTC.
kyra: Still seeing intermittent 502s for long-lived streams — likely due to cold KV cache on standby if we flip. Let's hold flip. Continue rate-limit + client changes.
cobalt-sre: Client-side jitter pushed, reconnect failures reduced to ~7%. Good improvement. Thank you.
oncall-amber: Can we also increase server-side idle timeout for websocket proxy to 60s from 30s for this tenant? That should reduce mid-stream tear-downs.
matt-lee: I can patch the gateway route config: `redwoodctl gateway set --tenant cobaltbridge --ws-timeout 60s` applying to eu-west only. Will do in 2m.
shaun: Reminder — any route/timeout changes should be coordinated with billing/SLAs (we're increasing resources for this tenant). Amber, file a quick change note.
oncall-amber: Filing change note in #incidents and tagging ops: `change: cobaltbridge temp ws-timeout 60s; tenant-rate-limit 50rps; monitoring hold`
eng-ops-bot: Change recorded: id chg-2026-0429-7 at 10:33 UTC.
matt-lee: Applied ws-timeout 60s to cobaltbridge in eu-west. Propagating.
kyra: After ws-timeout + rate-limit + restarts, error-rate down to ~1.3x baseline and 99th latency improving. Client reconnects now <3%.
cobalt-sre: We're seeing near-normal behavior. We'll keep clients at reduced concurrency for the next hour and run load tests later with you.
oncall-amber: Triage: cause appears to be a combination of tenant traffic spike + KV cache eviction pattern causing backend stalls and high GPU queueing in dedicated-cobalt. Mitigations applied: rate-limit, sysctl + restarts, raised ws timeout. Fallback route ready but not used.
shaun: Agree. Action items: - run postmortem & capacity plan for dedicated-cobalt (owner: kyra) - verify KV cache eviction policy and consider per-tenant cache caps (owner: devops-jay) - customer follow-up and SLA note (owner: oncall-amber).
kyra: I'll start a postmortem doc and link perf graphs. ETA for draft: EOD.
oncall-amber: Handoff: I'll be on light-watch for 1hr, then hand to morning oncall (mike) with status. If error-rate resurges >2x open page immediately.
cobalt-sre: Thanks team. Appreciate the quick coordination. We'll sync for a deeper runbook and testing tomorrow.
eng-ops-bot: Incident cleared to monitored state at 10:42 UTC. Severity downgraded to P2 for follow-up.
shaun: Good job.
oncall-amber: Closing thread in 30m unless we see regression. Leaving notes in postmortem doc. :thumbsup:
